premise: The Inheritance Evidence Laboratory has been forcing mitochondrial and chloroplast inheritance into nuclear Mendelian diagrams, using named disorders as definitions, and making chi-square decisions before the null model and data structure are established. The laboratory can be repaired only if inheritance route, biological case evidence, and statistical model evidence remain in separate compartments until a justified connection is needed.
mission: Follow Dr. Imani Reyes through seven connected locations. Separate nuclear from organelle inheritance, preserve qualified animal and plant parent-of-origin patterns, keep named disorders contextual, establish a chi-square goodness-of-fit model for categorical counts, distinguish observed from expected counts, build the chi-square statistic from category contributions, and finish with the correct degrees-of-freedom, significance, and reject or fail-to-reject decision logic.
finale: The evidence laboratory now keeps three forms of reasoning distinct and connected. Organelle genomes follow their own transmission routes, disorder cases illustrate specific mechanisms without defining broad categories, and chi-square conclusions arise from a defined null model, categorical observed and expected counts, a calculated statistic, degrees of freedom, and an explicit significance criterion.
learner_rule: Keep the three-compartment evidence tray visible. Identify whether a claim concerns inheritance route, biological case evidence, or statistical model evidence before using it to support a conclusion. Optional Quick Recall appears only three times.
route_orientation: This is one continuous west-to-east evidence-laboratory route. Begin at the west non-nuclear inheritance dock, pass through the animal mitochondrial corridor and plant organelle greenhouse, enter the central case archive, then continue through the statistics model bench, observed-expected calculation station, and final east decision console. The three-compartment evidence tray persists throughout and the statistical conclusion panel remains covered until the final room.

scenes.story_open: The final wing of the Heredity complex opens into the **Inheritance Evidence Laboratory**, and the first room makes the problem obvious before anyone speaks. On your **left**, an enormous blue-and-amber nuclear chromosome diagram covers a wall and sends every trait through a Mendelian segregation lane. Directly **ahead**, a stainless cytoplasmic dock holds transparent mitochondria and chloroplasts, each containing its own small genome token outside the nucleus. On your **right**, a branching channel distributes whole organelles into model daughter cells and gametes. Dr. Imani Reyes sets the **three-compartment evidence tray** on the central bench. The inheritance-route compartment is open, while the biological-case and statistical-model compartments remain closed. She tells you that this laboratory has been making one mistake repeatedly. It has treated every inherited trait as though the relevant DNA had to ride inside a nuclear chromosome.
story_paragraphs: The final wing of the Heredity complex opens into the **Inheritance Evidence Laboratory**, and the first room makes the problem obvious before anyone speaks. On your **left**, an enormous blue-and-amber nuclear chromosome diagram covers a wall and sends every trait through a Mendelian segregation lane. Directly **ahead**, a stainless cytoplasmic dock holds transparent mitochondria and chloroplasts, each containing its own small genome token outside the nucleus. On your **right**, a branching channel distributes whole organelles into model daughter cells and gametes. Dr. Imani Reyes sets the **three-compartment evidence tray** on the central bench. The inheritance-route compartment is open, while the biological-case and statistical-model compartments remain closed. She tells you that this laboratory has been making one mistake repeatedly. It has treated every inherited trait as though the relevant DNA had to ride inside a nuclear chromosome.

Imani brings the familiar **organelle inheritance model** beside the left wall. The blue and amber nuclear chromosomes move through a conventional segregation animation. Then she freezes them. In the transparent cytoplasm, glowing DNA tokens remain inside mitochondria and chloroplasts. She opens the center dock and names the broad relationship **Non-nuclear inheritance overview**. Some inherited traits can arise from genetic information outside the nuclear chromosome set because mitochondrial or chloroplast genomes can be transmitted independently of nuclear chromosomes. The word non-nuclear therefore identifies where the relevant genome resides. It does not mean the trait lacks a DNA basis, and it does not erase the role of the nucleus in the rest of the cell.

The center dock now advances one cell division. Nuclear chromosomes segregate along the left reference lane. At the same time, mitochondria and chloroplasts are distributed through the cytoplasm as organelles and organelle copies move into the daughter cells. Imani names the mechanism **Non-nuclear inheritance**. Traits encoded by mitochondrial or chloroplast DNA can show inheritance patterns that depart from standard Mendelian nuclear expectations because organelle transmission is not the same process as nuclear chromosome segregation. The real mitochondria and chloroplasts remain visible. Nothing is replaced by a mnemonic creature, and no allele tag is allowed to jump from the nucleus into an organelle merely to make the scene memorable.

On the right, the branching channel opens into four model gametes. The organelle tokens are partitioned among them with visible variation in how many copies enter each compartment. Imani labels the relationship **Organelle assortment**. Mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes do not segregate according to the nuclear chromosome Mendelian pattern displayed on the left wall. Their organelles and genome copies are partitioned through the cytoplasm into daughter cells and gametes. She keeps the nuclear reference wall lit so you can compare the mechanisms without confusing them. Nuclear chromosome segregation remains real biology. Organelle assortment is another real inheritance route operating through different cellular structures.

A technician tries to stamp NON-MENDELIAN on every object in the right channel and then remove the DNA labels. Imani stops the machine. Non-nuclear inheritance does not mean mysterious inheritance without genes. The inherited information is still DNA. The distinction concerns mitochondrial or chloroplast genomes and their transmission through cytoplasmic organelles. She places one mitochondrial DNA token and one chloroplast DNA token into the first compartment of the evidence tray. The tray now records what kind of inheritance route is being examined before any parent-of-origin pattern is discussed.

The lab lights dim except for three anchors. The nuclear chromosome reference remains on the left, the organelle genome dock remains directly ahead, and the organelle assortment channel remains on the right. Imani asks you to reconstruct the room using only those anchors. If a trait depends on DNA in a mitochondrial or chloroplast genome, its transmission can follow the distribution of those organelles through cells and gametes. That is why its inheritance does not have to match a nuclear Mendelian ratio. The first optional Quick Recall can now occur because the mechanism has already been seen and named.

A narrow animal-fertilization corridor opens beyond the right channel. Imani slides the evidence tray forward while leaving the nuclear reference diagram behind. The next question is more specific. If mitochondrial genomes follow an organelle route, which parent usually contributes the mitochondrial pool in a typical animal fertilization model. The route cannot be answered by the phrase non-nuclear alone. You will have to follow the organelles into the zygote.
scenes.story_close: The laboratory now separates nuclear chromosome inheritance from organelle-genome transmission. The evidence tray carries that distinction into a typical animal mitochondrial route.

scenes.story_open: The corridor bends into the **Mitochondrial Inheritance Route**. On your **left**, a sperm model reaches a fertilization window with its nuclear chromosome contribution highlighted separately from its mitochondrial contribution. Directly **ahead**, a large transparent zygote chamber waits beside an egg model packed with cytoplasm and many mitochondria. On your **right**, a family route branches through several generations under a bright sign that reads USUALLY and TYPICALLY. Imani places the inheritance-route compartment of the **three-compartment evidence tray** beside the chamber and slides the **organelle inheritance model** into the center. The layout makes the question physical. You are following the origin of the zygote mitochondrial pool, not asking which parent contributed nuclear chromosomes.
story_paragraphs: The corridor bends into the **Mitochondrial Inheritance Route**. On your **left**, a sperm model reaches a fertilization window with its nuclear chromosome contribution highlighted separately from its mitochondrial contribution. Directly **ahead**, a large transparent zygote chamber waits beside an egg model packed with cytoplasm and many mitochondria. On your **right**, a family route branches through several generations under a bright sign that reads USUALLY and TYPICALLY. Imani places the inheritance-route compartment of the **three-compartment evidence tray** beside the chamber and slides the **organelle inheritance model** into the center. The layout makes the question physical. You are following the origin of the zygote mitochondrial pool, not asking which parent contributed nuclear chromosomes.

Imani opens the egg membrane on the model and lets its cytoplasm flow into the central zygote chamber. Numerous mitochondrial tokens enter with it. The sperm model contributes its nuclear material through a separate track, while the typical mitochondrial pool in the zygote is built primarily from mitochondria transmitted through the egg. Only after the zygote contains that pool does Imani name **Animal mitochondrial inheritance**. In animals, mitochondrial DNA is usually transmitted through the egg much more commonly than through sperm, so mitochondrial-DNA traits are typically maternally inherited. The parent-of-origin pattern follows the organelle contribution in this model.

The family route on the right now activates. A person who transmits mitochondria through eggs can pass a mitochondrial-DNA variant into descendants through those eggs. The route traces that variant across generations without moving it onto an X chromosome, an autosome, or a Y chromosome. Imani points back to the first room. Mitochondrial inheritance is non-nuclear because the relevant genome is in mitochondria. Its typical maternal pattern in animals comes from the usual route of mitochondrial contribution to the zygote. These are connected ideas, yet they answer two different questions about location and parent of origin.

A metal arm tries to remove the USUALLY sign and replace it with ALWAYS. Imani locks the arm. The qualifier remains attached to every branch. Biological transmission has exceptions, and the locked science for this route describes the usual or typical animal pattern. The story therefore cannot become a universal rule claiming that every animal mitochondrial genome in every circumstance must come from one parent. The bright qualifier is part of the scientific model, not a decorative disclaimer added after the fact.

Imani then places a chloroplast token next to the family route. It does not enter. This room is about typical **animal mitochondrial inheritance**. The plant organelle question is still unresolved. Chloroplast inheritance cannot be imported automatically from an animal mitochondrial pattern, and even plant mitochondrial transmission must be treated in its own species-dependent context. She closes the animal route compartment of the evidence tray with the phrase typical maternal mitochondrial inheritance visible through the glass.

To check the distinction, she covers the family tree and leaves only the sperm window, zygote chamber, and egg mitochondrial pool visible. You can still explain the typical parent-of-origin pattern from the biological route. The zygote receives most of the mitochondrial pool through the egg in the typical animal model, so mitochondrial-DNA traits are commonly maternally inherited. The explanation does not depend on memorizing a family-tree silhouette. It depends on following the organelles into the zygote.

A greenhouse-style comparison room opens ahead. Three plant transmission channels are visible through the glass, one entering through an ovule route, one through a pollen route, and one through both. Imani carries the evidence tray into that room with the animal qualifier still visible. The next scene will test whether you can preserve a common pattern while leaving room for species variation.
scenes.story_close: The animal route now shows typical maternal mitochondrial inheritance without converting the common pattern into an absolute rule. The next room compares plant organelle routes directly.

On your **left**, a pollen-side branch carries paternal and biparental possibility cards toward a model seed. Directly **ahead**, a species-comparison table holds mitochondria and chloroplasts from several plants, each with its organelle genome token clearly visible. story_paragraphs: The next door opens into the **Plant Organelle Inheritance Route**, a glass-roofed comparison room built around three living transmission channels. On your **left**, a pollen-side branch carries paternal and biparental possibility cards toward a model seed. Directly **ahead**, a species-comparison table holds mitochondria and chloroplasts from several plants, each with its organelle genome token clearly visible. On your **right**, a broad ovule-side branch carries many of the example organelle genomes into the next generation. Imani sets the **organelle inheritance model** beside the center table and places the animal mitochondrial card from the previous room at the far edge for comparison. The plant room begins with three open doors because the answer cannot be assumed before the species pattern is known.

Imani moves the first set of plant tokens through the center table. In many examples, mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes travel predominantly through the ovule contribution. The right branch brightens, and she names **Plant organelle inheritance**. In many plants, mitochondria and chloroplasts are transmitted predominantly through the ovule, so traits encoded by those organelle genomes are often maternally inherited. The word often remains visible beside the branch. The route describes a common pattern across many plant systems while preserving the fact that organelle transmission varies among species.

She then activates the left branch. A paternal route lights for one comparison card, and a biparental route lights for another. The right route does not disappear. Imani wants all three possibilities visible at the same time because the memory target is a qualified biological pattern. Plant organelle inheritance can differ across species and organelles. Some patterns are predominantly maternal, some show paternal contribution, and some include biparental transmission. The palace therefore encodes the common ovule-associated pattern with an open comparison structure, not with a locked one-way gate.

The evidence tray now contains two route cards. The animal card says mitochondrial DNA is usually transmitted through the egg in typical animal models. The plant card says mitochondria and chloroplasts in many plants are transmitted predominantly through the ovule and are often maternally inherited. Imani keeps the wording separate. A learner who remembers only maternal inheritance has lost the scientific distinction. The animal statement concerns mitochondria and a typical animal route. The plant statement concerns mitochondria and chloroplasts across plant species with more visible transmission variation.

A technician wheels in a large label reading MATERNAL INHERITANCE and tries to cover all three channels. Imani folds the label and places it under the right branch only. The biological route must remain richer than the shortcut. The left branch stays open for paternal and biparental possibilities. This prevents a vivid palace image from becoming scientifically stronger than the evidence supports. Memorable structure is useful only when the qualifiers survive with the term.

Imani asks you to point to the three physical anchors in order. Paternal or biparental possibility remains on the left. Species-dependent organelle comparison remains in the center. Often-maternal transmission through the ovule remains on the right. From those anchors, you can reconstruct the statement without needing a slogan. Many plants show predominantly ovule-associated organelle transmission, and plant organelle inheritance varies among species. The evidence tray closes the route compartment with both the animal and plant patterns still visible through separate windows.

The greenhouse exit leads into a climate-controlled archive. Two named disorder files sit on opposite walls, while a central index contains the broader categories genetic disorder and pathogenic variant. Imani shifts the evidence tray so the second compartment, biological case evidence, is now open. The next room will use concrete human disease examples, but the examples will not be allowed to define an entire inheritance category.

scenes.story_open: The **Inheritance Case Archive** is quieter than the organelle rooms. On your **left**, a sealed drawer contains a Tay-Sachs case file with a chromosome diagram, a HEXA gene card, a lysosomal enzyme panel, and a neuron model. Directly **ahead**, the central index has two empty slots labeled **Genetic disorder** and **Pathogenic variant**. On your **right**, a separate sickle cell disease drawer contains an HBB gene card, hemoglobin molecules, red blood cells, and a low-oxygen chamber. Imani opens the biological-case compartment of the **three-compartment evidence tray** and keeps the inheritance-route compartment closed beside it. She tells you that named diseases can clarify mechanisms, but a memorable disease example must never become the definition of recessive inheritance, genetic variation, or genetic disorder itself.
story_paragraphs: The **Inheritance Case Archive** is quieter than the organelle rooms. On your **left**, a sealed drawer contains a Tay-Sachs case file with a chromosome diagram, a HEXA gene card, a lysosomal enzyme panel, and a neuron model. Directly **ahead**, the central index has two empty slots labeled **Genetic disorder** and **Pathogenic variant**. On your **right**, a separate sickle cell disease drawer contains an HBB gene card, hemoglobin molecules, red blood cells, and a low-oxygen chamber. Imani opens the biological-case compartment of the **three-compartment evidence tray** and keeps the inheritance-route compartment closed beside it. She tells you that named diseases can clarify mechanisms, but a memorable disease example must never become the definition of recessive inheritance, genetic variation, or genetic disorder itself.

Imani begins at the center index. She places many kinds of evidence cards under **Genetic disorder**. Some involve a single gene, some involve chromosome changes, some involve multiple genes, and some involve environmental contributions interacting with genetic variation. A genetic disorder is a disease or condition in which genetic variation contributes causally to phenotype. The broad category therefore does not require one inheritance pattern or one molecular mechanism. The index remains larger than either case drawer so the physical space itself prevents the examples from swallowing the category.

The second slot receives the term **Pathogenic variant**. Imani places one DNA sequence card there only after attaching an evidence tag showing that the variant contributes to disease. A pathogenic variant is a DNA sequence variant with evidence supporting a disease-contributing role. She removes an older card labeled mutated allele from the general index because that phrase can be less precise for clinical classification. The important memory is not a new euphemism. It is the evidence rule. A sequence difference becomes classified as pathogenic when evidence supports that disease contribution.

The left drawer opens. Imani labels it **Tay-Sachs disease example**. The file traces pathogenic HEXA variants through an autosomal recessive inheritance model. The molecular panel shows severe deficiency of beta-hexosaminidase A activity, followed by progressive accumulation of material that contributes to neurodegeneration. Imani keeps the enzyme meter above zero because the locked science says severe deficiency, not an absolute requirement for complete enzyme absence in every case. The disorder file therefore teaches one correct mechanism while remaining an example of autosomal recessive inheritance, not the definition of autosomal recessive inheritance.

The right drawer opens independently. Imani labels it **Sickle cell disease example**. Pathogenic HBB variants produce hemoglobin S in an autosomal recessive disorder. In the low-oxygen chamber, hemoglobin S molecules polymerize, changing red blood cell shape and impairing function. The red cells deform because of the hemoglobin behavior under low-oxygen conditions in the model. Imani keeps this case separate from Tay-Sachs. Both can be discussed with autosomal recessive inheritance, yet their genes, proteins, cell biology, and disease mechanisms are different.

A filing machine tries to stamp RECESSIVE DISORDER across both drawers and then copy that label onto the center definition of genetic disorder. Imani disables it. The inheritance pattern of a particular example cannot define the larger category. A genetic disorder can arise through many genetic architectures. A pathogenic variant is an evidence-based classification of a DNA sequence variant. Tay-Sachs disease and sickle cell disease are specific examples that help students connect genotype, molecular mechanism, and phenotype. The archive works only when those levels stay separate.

Imani asks you to close both case drawers and keep the central index visible. You can still define genetic disorder and pathogenic variant without naming either disease. Then she reopens the drawers so the molecular details can serve as concrete applications. The evidence tray records the case files in its second compartment and locks them there. No disorder example will be carried into the statistical model as though the example itself were a universal expected ratio.

At the far end of the archive, the floor changes from case-file shelves to a quantitative workbench. Four empty category bins sit beneath a card labeled null model. A dark **chi-square evidence console** waits under a protective cover. Imani closes the biological-case compartment and opens the statistical-model compartment. The final three rooms will ask a different question. Given a specified inheritance model and categorical count data, how much disagreement between observation and expectation is compatible with sampling variation under that model.
scenes.story_close: The archive now keeps broad genetic concepts separate from illustrative disorder cases. The evidence tray shifts to its statistical-model compartment for chi-square reasoning.

scenes.story_open: The **Chi-Square Model Bench** occupies a bright statistics room with three fixed stations. On your **left**, a null-model rack holds expected category proportions for a specified inheritance model. Directly **ahead**, the **chi-square evidence console** has four categorical bins and the formula χ² = Σ((O−E)²/E) etched across its glass cover. On your **right**, a gate admits only category-count cards while a tray of continuous measurements remains outside the lane. Imani places the statistical-model compartment of the **three-compartment evidence tray** beside the console. The console stays locked. Before a number can be calculated, the model and the type of data must be clear.
story_paragraphs: The **Chi-Square Model Bench** occupies a bright statistics room with three fixed stations. On your **left**, a null-model rack holds expected category proportions for a specified inheritance model. Directly **ahead**, the **chi-square evidence console** has four categorical bins and the formula χ² = Σ((O−E)²/E) etched across its glass cover. On your **right**, a gate admits only category-count cards while a tray of continuous measurements remains outside the lane. Imani places the statistical-model compartment of the **three-compartment evidence tray** beside the console. The console stays locked. Before a number can be calculated, the model and the type of data must be clear.

Imani selects a fixed-proportion inheritance model from the left rack. The model supplies expected proportions for the outcome categories. She does not claim that the model is true merely because it has been chosen as a null model. It is the reference explanation being evaluated. She converts the expected proportions into expected counts for the sample size and places those counts in covered slots. Only then does she introduce **Chi-square hypothesis testing**. In this workflow, observed and expected categorical counts are compared through χ² = Σ((O−E)²/E), and the resulting statistic will later be evaluated with degrees of freedom and a significance criterion before any hypothesis decision is made.

The center cover rises one section. Imani names the **Chi-square goodness-of-fit test**. Its question is whether the observed categorical counts differ from the model-based expected counts by more than would be expected from sampling variation under the null hypothesis. She points to the phrase under the null hypothesis on the model rack. The procedure does not ask whether the observed data are perfectly identical to expectation. Random samples commonly deviate from exact expected proportions. The statistical test evaluates how large the deviations are relative to the model and expected category sizes.

On the right, the data-type gate tests several inputs. Cards labeled purple offspring, white offspring, recombinant class, parental class, and phenotype category pass through because they can be represented as category frequencies. A card containing individual plant heights remains outside. Imani names the rule **Chi-square uses categorical counts**. The Unit 5 goodness-of-fit procedure works with categorical counts or frequencies. Continuous measurements are not entered directly into this particular workflow as though they were category counts. A separate statistical method might be appropriate for a different data structure, but that question is outside this palace scene.

A technician tries to feed percentages directly into the center formula without showing the sample size or category counts. Imani returns the cards to the left rack. Expected proportions are useful because they generate expected counts for the actual sample size. The chi-square calculation compares count with count. She also stops another technician from opening the final decision panel. The current room cannot reject or fail to reject anything yet. Degrees of freedom and a significance criterion have not been supplied, so the correct scientific action is to keep the conclusion covered.

Imani uncovers the three compartments of the evidence tray for a moment. Inheritance route evidence answered how genomes were transmitted. Case evidence illustrated specific genotype-to-phenotype mechanisms. Statistical model evidence asks whether categorical observations are sufficiently consistent with a specified null model. The three kinds of reasoning can support one larger genetics investigation, yet none is interchangeable with another. That separation is why the final laboratory can remain memorable without reducing every genetics question to a single procedure.

The second optional Quick Recall appears only now. Imani points to the right gate and asks what kinds of data the Unit 5 chi-square goodness-of-fit procedure compares. Once you retrieve categorical counts or frequencies, the gate opens. The console then rolls forward to the next room, where the observed and expected columns will be exposed and each category will contribute to the total χ² statistic.

scenes.story_open: The console rolls into the **Observed–Expected Calculation Station** and splits into three vertical sections. On your **left**, the observed column contains the categorical frequencies actually recorded in the study. Directly **ahead**, a glass calculator displays one category at a time beneath the expression (O−E)²/E. On your **right**, the expected column contains frequencies predicted by the null model from the total sample size and specified expected proportions. Imani locks the **three-compartment evidence tray** beside the station and leaves only the statistical-model compartment open. The physical separation is strict because observed and expected counts come from different sources of evidence.
story_paragraphs: The console rolls into the **Observed–Expected Calculation Station** and splits into three vertical sections. On your **left**, the observed column contains the categorical frequencies actually recorded in the study. Directly **ahead**, a glass calculator displays one category at a time beneath the expression (O−E)²/E. On your **right**, the expected column contains frequencies predicted by the null model from the total sample size and specified expected proportions. Imani locks the **three-compartment evidence tray** beside the station and leaves only the statistical-model compartment open. The physical separation is strict because observed and expected counts come from different sources of evidence.

Imani uncovers the left column and names **Observed count (O)**. These are the category frequencies actually recorded in the data. A counter above each bin is linked to the collected sample, not to the inheritance model. She then uncovers the right column and names **Expected count (E)**. These are the category frequencies predicted by the null model, often calculated from the total sample size and the expected proportions specified by that model. The two columns may contain similar numbers, but similarity does not make them the same kind of quantity.

The center calculator takes one observed value and its corresponding expected value. It subtracts E from O, squares the difference, and divides by E. Imani names this category-level quantity **Chi-square contribution**. Each category contributes (O−E)²/E to the total χ². Squaring removes the sign of the difference, so deviations above and below expectation do not cancel one another. Dividing by E scales the discrepancy relative to the expected size of that category. The machine preserves the contribution in a transparent compartment before moving to the next category.

Imani demonstrates the workflow with the arithmetic hidden behind the glass. You can see O enter from the left and E enter from the right. The calculator performs the operation and outputs one nonnegative contribution. The palace is teaching the structure of the calculation, while full arithmetic practice remains for Challenge Lab. The important memory is the source and role of each quantity. O is observed from data. E is expected from the null model. Each pair produces a category contribution, and the contributions are summed to form the overall χ² statistic.

A lab assistant tries to swap the column headers. The console rejects the change. An expected count cannot become observed merely because it looks plausible, and an observed count cannot be treated as the model prediction. Imani traces a line from the left column back to the collected data cards and a separate line from the right column back to the null-model rack in the previous room. Those two provenance lines remain visible while every calculation is performed.

The final category contribution drops into the center sum chamber. The console adds all the category contributions and displays one χ² statistic. Imani immediately covers the conclusion lights again. A large χ² indicates greater overall disagreement between observed and expected counts, but the number by itself does not yet supply the formal hypothesis decision. Its interpretation depends on the degrees of freedom and the chosen significance criterion. The next room contains those controls.

Before leaving, Imani asks you to redraw the station from memory. Observed count belongs on the left and comes from recorded data. Expected count belongs on the right and comes from the null model. The center transforms each matched pair through (O−E)²/E, then sums the contributions. If those three anchors are preserved, the formula no longer floats as an arbitrary sequence of symbols. It is a structured comparison of data against a model.

The far wall slides open to reveal the **Chi-Square Decision Console**. A degrees-of-freedom selector and critical-value table stand on the left, the calculated χ² enters the center, and two conclusion lamps wait on the right. Imani carries the summed statistic forward without changing any observed or expected count. The next room will decide what the statistic means under the chosen criterion.

story_paragraphs: The final door opens onto the **Chi-Square Decision Console**. On your **left**, a control bank displays the number of outcome categories, a degrees-of-freedom selector, a significance-level dial, and a critical-value table. Directly **ahead**, the χ² statistic from the previous station glows inside the central console. On your **right**, two conclusion lamps are mounted above separate doors. One reads REJECT THE NULL. The other reads FAIL TO REJECT THE NULL. There is no third door labeled ACCEPT THE NULL. Imani places the complete **three-compartment evidence tray** beneath the controls and uncovers every compartment. The laboratory can now connect inheritance mechanism, biological evidence, and statistical evidence without confusing the jobs of those evidence types.

Imani starts at the left selector and names **Degrees of freedom for AP goodness-of-fit**. For the AP goodness-of-fit setup used here, where expected proportions are fixed and no additional parameters are estimated from the data, degrees of freedom equal the number of outcome categories minus one. She keeps the task context printed above the selector. The formula is not offered as a universal rule for every chi-square procedure. It belongs to this fixed-proportion goodness-of-fit setup.

Next she turns the significance-level dial and selects an alpha criterion. The critical-value table responds to both alpha and degrees of freedom. Imani names the **Chi-square critical value**. A chi-square critical value depends on the chosen significance level and degrees of freedom and provides a threshold against which the calculated statistic can be evaluated. The table does not come from the observed counts themselves. It is part of the inferential decision framework supplied after the test setup is known.

A second display shows the corresponding probability interpretation, and Imani names **p-value and significance level**. A p-value describes how extreme a test statistic at least as large as the observed one would be under the null model. The chosen alpha, such as 0.05, is the significance threshold used for the decision. Imani removes a false sign claiming that alpha of 0.05 means there is a 95 percent probability the null hypothesis is true. The console cannot produce that statement because it is not what the p-value or alpha means.

The calculated χ² now enters the center decision track. One route compares the statistic with the relevant critical value. Another route compares the p-value with alpha. Both routes feed the same decision panel. Imani names the final relationship **Reject or fail to reject the null**. When the evidence exceeds the chosen threshold, the null hypothesis is rejected at that significance level. When it does not, the correct conclusion is to fail to reject the null hypothesis. The second outcome leaves the null model plausible under the available evidence. It does not prove the null model true.

A technician rolls in an ACCEPTED stamp. The right panel has no slot for it. Imani sends it back to storage. A nonsignificant result can occur when the observed data are reasonably compatible with the null model, when the sample is limited, or when the test lacks enough evidence to detect a departure. The workflow therefore protects the wording of the conclusion. Fail to reject is a statement about the available evidence under the chosen criterion. It is not a declaration that the null has been verified as fact.

The three-compartment evidence tray now becomes the final memory map for Unit 5. The inheritance-route compartment holds nuclear and organelle transmission distinctions, including qualified animal and plant parent-of-origin patterns. The biological-case compartment holds contextual disease examples and evidence-based variant language. The statistical-model compartment holds the null model, categorical observed and expected counts, χ² calculation, degrees of freedom, decision threshold, and final conclusion. Each compartment answers a different question, and the complete investigation becomes stronger because those questions remain distinguishable.

The third optional Quick Recall appears at the decision panel. Imani points to the two illuminated doors and asks for the correct hypothesis-decision phrases. Once you retrieve **Reject or fail to reject the null**, the console records the answer and closes the false accept-null slot permanently. She then asks you to replay the full statistical route. Define the null model, obtain expected categorical counts, compare them with observed counts, compute category contributions and χ², determine the relevant degrees of freedom and criterion, then state the evidence-based decision.

Imani closes the laboratory by sliding the three-compartment evidence tray into the gold generation ledger cabinet. The Unit 5 route can now be reconstructed from chromosomes and meiosis through inheritance models, probability, non-Mendelian mechanisms, linkage mapping, organelle inheritance, and statistical evidence. The final room does not turn chi-square into a verdict machine. It preserves a scientific habit. Start with a model, keep observations separate from expectations, calculate from defined quantities, apply the correct criterion, and state only the conclusion the evidence supports.
